Distribution. Known only from the type locality. Relationships. The new species appears to belong to a lineage of montane Mexican and Central American species that include the aforementioned E. varius, as well as E. maculicollis (Spinola), E. whiteheadi Ekis, E. villicus (Gorham), E. absconditus Rifkind and the three taxa described directly below. They share a similar facies, rather loosely composed antennal club, a broad ocular insertion, and shining, finely punctulate or shallowly roughened and sparsely setose elytra, the latter often marked with three or four sets of pale transverse bands and / or maculae. Except for the Central American species, they are very rarely collected, and no doubt other members of the group await discovery in the mountain forests of México.
